label: Xl Recordings
release_notes: Fifth album from the Dublin band, after Romance (2024). Produced by James Ford, who also made Romance. Metacritic score 85 from 19 reviews.

Most of it was recorded at Decoy Studios in Suffolk, with additional sessions at Narcissus Studios in London (February 2025 to March 2026). Grian Chatten recorded his vocals separately with Ford in Palermo, Sicily. Marta Salogni engineered; Matt Colton mastered (Wikipedia).
Grian Chatten - vocals, guitar; Carlos O'Connell - guitar, synths; Conor Curley - guitar; Conor Deegan - bass; Tom Coll - drums.
Rosalía guests on Where Is Gone?, the band's first guest vocalist on a record. Strings arranged by Chatten, Richard Jones, Laura Moody and Elysian Collective.
Singles: Marianne (Aug. 18), Tongue (Sept. 30) and Where Is Gone? (Oct. 12). 11 tracks, about 44 minutes. Released Oct. 16, 2026.
Reviews (Guardian, NME, Pitchfork, AllMusic) hear synths, strings and electronics over guitars, with comparisons to The Cure, Depeche Mode, New Order and Massive Attack.

draft_comment: Dublin post-punk gone synth-heavy, string-laced and stadium-sized, again with James Ford and a Rosalía duet. Critics hear Depeche Mode, The Cure and New Order. Tongue and Japan are FCC.

tracks.title: Six Shot Morning
tracks.notes: Opener. Teased Aug. 15; live debut in Cádiz in August. Mechanical Depeche Mode death march (NME); chugging bassline and searching synths (AllMusic).

tracks.title: Marianne
tracks.notes: Lead single (Aug. 18), with a Dave Meyers video. Live debut in Cádiz in August. Strings arranged by Chatten, Richard Jones, Laura Moody and Elysian Collective. Cyborg-meets-symphony balladry (NME); spiralling strings (Guardian).

tracks.title: Mimesis
tracks.notes: Synth-pop noir (NME); a New Order-style bassline (Guardian).

tracks.title: Happy For You
tracks.notes: Debuted live at Leeds Festival, Aug. 29. A Cure-like guitar twang (Guardian); a massive guitar drop (AllMusic).

tracks.title: Demolition
tracks.notes: Album highlight, with fuzzy electronica (NME); a grunge attack (Guardian).

tracks.title: Tongue
tracks.notes: Second single (Sept. 30), with a New York-shot video directed by PHC (John Angus Stewart). In FCC Edit Needed. Trip-hop gloom (NME); the oddest track on the album (AllMusic).

tracks.title: One Man
tracks.notes: Second-longest track. Breathy and elegiac (NME); starts the album's run of tender songs (AllMusic).

tracks.title: Where Is Gone? (with ROSALÍA)
tracks.notes: Features Rosalía, the band's first guest vocalist. Third single (Oct. 12). Longest track. A Morricone-style ballad and would-be Bond theme (NME, Guardian). No FCC words in the English lyrics posted; Spanish checked for common swear words.

tracks.title: Japan
tracks.notes: Bittersweet acoustic singalong (NME). Bandcamp lists 3:14; Wikipedia lists 3:15.

sources: Lyrics screened on Genius (counts only): all 11 tracks. FCC words on tracks 6 and 10.
